questions.cardText:
[Art History] Who was the subject of Edvard Munch’s painting “The Scream”?
A. Munch himself
B. A friend of Munch’s
C. A passerby Munch saw on a bridge
Answer: A. Suffering from a panic attack, Munch described the inspiration for the painting as a moment of overwhelming terror while he was walking during a sunset. The iconic image with an agonized expression inspired one of the most popular emojis people use today.
questions.de: Edvard Munch stützte „Der Schrei“ auf ein eigenes Erlebnis bei einem Spaziergang im Sonnenuntergang, als sich die Wolken blutrot färbten: Was spürte er nach eigenen Worten durch die Natur gehen?
questions.en: Edvard Munch based “The Scream” on his own experience on a walk at sunset, when the clouds turned blood red: what did he say he sensed passing through nature?
questions.notes: The card's claim that the figure is Munch himself is an interpretation (Wikipedia calls it the agonized face representing existential dread; his diary describes his own experience); 'panic attack' is not in the source. Reworked to the documented fact from Munch's diary: he sensed an 'infinite scream passing through nature'.

questions.cardText:
[Physiology and Anatomy] What is the largest bone in the human body?
A. Femur B. Tibia C. Humerus
Answer: A. The femur is often found in fossilized remains and can provide significant information about ancient humans and animals, such as their posture, locomotion, and overall health.
questions.de: Was ist der größte Knochen des menschlichen Körpers?
questions.en: What is the largest bone in the human body?

timeline.labelEn: Andreas Vesalius publishes De humani corporis fabrica, the founding work of modern human anatomy
timeline.labelDe: Andreas Vesalius veröffentlicht „De humani corporis fabrica“, das Gründungswerk der modernen Anatomie des Menschen

questions.notes: Wikipedia: the femur is the largest, thickest and longest bone in the human body. Timeline: no date of its own; Vesalius's Fabrica (June 1543).
